1	# Task 10: Walking spider from primitives
2	
3	Build a single-page browser app with the provided framework, served by vite, rendering to the canvas with id #app. Show a spider made only from simple geometric shapes (a body made of two or more primitives and eight jointed legs, each leg having at least two segments) walking in place on a flat ground plane. The legs must move in an alternating gait: legs on opposite diagonals move together, and each leg visibly lifts, swings forward and plants again. The body should bob slightly with each step. The motion must loop seamlessly with a period of about 2 seconds and run continuously without user input. Use a neutral studio-style backdrop with soft lighting and shadows so the shape reads clearly from a three-quarter camera that frames the whole spider. Do not load external model files.
4	
5	## Rendering contract (all tasks)
6	
7	- Draw into the existing `<canvas id="app">` (640x360 CSS pixels, device pixel ratio 1). Do not resize it or create another canvas.
8	- Render continuously with `requestAnimationFrame`. When the first frame has been drawn set `window.__EVAL_READY__ = true`.
9	- No network access: load assets only from `/assets/...` (served from `public/assets`). Do not import from CDNs.
10	- Code goes in `src/` (TypeScript, strict). The entry is `src/main.ts`. It must pass `typecheck` and build with `vite build`.
11	- When you are done, call `finish`.

content.thinking:
Since Euler rotation order is ambiguous, I'm structuring each leg with a static outer group for yaw and a nested inner group for the swing motion, keeping the two rotations isolated to avoid order-dependent artifacts.

For the knee I'll stick with single-axis z rotation, and for leg geometry I'll orient cylinders along the X axis using a static quarter-turn rotation so segments extend outward correctly -- with the hip pitch set to lift the coxa up before the femur angles outward and the tibia drops back down into the resting spider pose.

Now I'm working through the leg kinematics numerically: computing femur and tibia positions given hip height and joint angles to see where the foot lands, and realizing that with fixed-angle poses the planted foot will slide relative to the ground as the body bobs, so I actually need a proper IK approach to keep the stance foot stationary in world space while the leg swings.

I'm setting this up as analytical inverse kinematics instead — a yaw angle for the hip's outward swing direction plus a planar two-link solve in the vertical plane, so that given a target foot position on the ground relative to the bobbing body, I can derive the exact hip and knee angles needed to reach it.

For the gait pattern, each foot moves between a back and front stance offset along the body axis, with legs grouped into diagonal pairs (alternating tetrapod style) so opposite diagonals swing together. Within each cycle, half the time is stance (foot sliding backward along the ground to push the body forward) and half is swing (foot lifting with an eased arc from back to front).

I'm setting forward as +Z with a three-quarter camera view, adding a subtle body bob tied to twice the step frequency since each diagonal group plants once per period, and working out the hip yaw rotation so each leg's static outward angle correctly rotates its local forward direction using right-handed Y-axis convention.

I'll assume the standard right-handed, y-up convention since I can't verify in a browser, and apply the same rotation convention consistently for both the static hip yaw and the dynamic swing rotation so the foot IK and leg orientation stay matched without mirroring errors.

I'm structuring the leg hierarchy as nested groups: a static legRoot with position and yaw rotation, a dynamic yaw group, then a dynamic pitch group containing the coxa ball joint and femur cylinder, followed by a knee group with the tibia and foot sphere. For the IK, I'm rotating the world-space foot target into the root's local frame by negating the hip yaw angle to get local coordinates.

Now I'm working out the yaw angle from the local foot direction using atan2, then collapsing the horizontal and vertical offsets into a planar two-link problem to solve for the femur and knee angles.

For the knee, I compute the clamped target distance, apply the law of cosines to get the knee bend angle (keeping it negative since spider legs bend downward), then derive the femur's angle by combining the direction to the target with the correction from the knee offset.

Now I'm working out actual numbers: femur length 0.9, tibia 1.4, with the body's abdomen radius around 0.55 and hip joints offset about 0.45 from center. Checking the rest-pose foot position at radius 1.9 gives a horizontal reach of 1.45 from the hip, and I'm verifying this distance falls within the valid range so the leg doesn't overextend.

Working through the law of cosines, I get β around -94° and α around 34°, meaning the femur angles upward and the knee bends downward — giving that spidery look I want. For hip placement, I'm laying out four leg pairs symmetrically along the body's z-axis at roughly z = 0.4, 0.15, -0.1, -0.35, each offset ±0.35 in x, with a stride amplitude of 0.35 and lift height of 0.4 for the walking cycle.

Now I'm defining each leg's outward direction vector by mirroring the right-side directions across x for the left side, then computing the rest foot targets as the hip position plus that direction scaled out 1.5 units, with stride offset applied along the body's forward axis — letting the IK solver handle the rest.

I'm grouping legs diagonally for the gait pattern, assigning phase offsets so opposite corners swing together, and defining the foot height curve using a smoothstep ease during swing (lift following a sine arc) and a linear slide during stance. I'm also deciding to skip abdomen sway for simplicity and treating the cephalothorax as a scaled ellipsoid using a vector size parameter.

Now I'm assembling the body from a cephalothorax ellipsoid, a tilted abdomen ellipsoid behind it, small glossy black spheres for eyes, and small cones for fangs, while skipping any extra pattern details on the abdomen. I'm then working out camera placement for a three-quarter front-right view, checking that the field of view comfortably frames the leg span and body length at the chosen distance, and setting up a light grey studio backdrop color.

For the environment I'm considering a large ground plane blending into the background, possibly with fog to soften the horizon, but I'm leaning toward just using the recommended "product-studio" lighting/backdrop preset instead of building it manually, weighing whether it already includes the ground plane and camera setup or if I still need to add my own.
